findings.issue: endSession issues one IndexedDB get per hand up to session.handsPlayed, which parseSessionRecord bounds only by MAX_SESSION_COUNT (1e9), and holds all of them in one readwrite transaction.
findings.evidence: A hand-edited sessions record (local IndexedDB, same origin: only the user themselves can write it) with handsPlayed near 1e9 -> ended() loop issues ~1e9 get requests -> tab stalls or runs out of memory when ending the session. No cross-user or remote path; impact is self-inflicted denial of service.
findings.fix: Optional: no change needed. If wanted, read with a key-range cursor (IDBKeyRange.bound([sessionId,1],[sessionId,Infinity])) so cost is bounded by records that actually exist rather than the claimed count.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR. parseSessionReport's new style check is sound: every count goes through isWhole (rejects NaN, Infinity, non-integers, negatives), handsDealt is 1..handsPlayed, and the part <= whole chain (voluntary<=dealt, preflopRaised<=voluntary, sawFlop<=dealt, showdowns<=sawFlop, showdownsWon<=showdowns) blocks impossible percentages. statTenths returns null when the whole is 0, so there is no division by zero. postflopAggressive/postflopCalls are only bounded by MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so the aggression sum could lose precision, but it only affects a displayed percentage on tampered data. In endSession, hand records are untrusted; each one goes through parseHandRecord, and invalid or missing records are skipped (fail-safe). The session record still fails closed and aborts the transaction. All report text renders through React text nodes. There is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML and no inline styles, and data-label values come from a fixed map. The healthy-ranges JSON ships with the code and is validated at import. No new dependencies, network calls, secrets or randomness.
